title: Browsing a 1990s software store
provenance_type: stock/archive scouting report plus one acquired archival original (real camcorder footage, 1995; not a reenactment and not AI-generated)

active_picture.note: 4:3 picture pillarboxed inside the 854x480 container (ffmpeg cropdetect). A 1080p timeline needs about a 2.25x upscale or an authored archival frame treatment; do not stretch to 16:9.

media_note: duration_seconds, dimensions and fps are ffprobe values for the acquired original source/1995-08-23_compusa-norwalk_dan-lynch_original.mp4 (the whole 230.6 s file), not for the selected segment. The candidate report remains the ticket's named variant.

selected_segment.note: Checked against the real file: the in point holds (soft; about 00:02:16.3 is cleaner), the scouted out point does not. The browse ends about 00:02:22.5 and 02:23-02:24 becomes a two-man handshake. The recommended 6.5 s is under the ticket's preferred 8-12 s; the choice is an editorial review question. No cut was rendered.

notes: Rights, recorded exactly: the Internet Archive item page states CC0 1.0 Universal; that CC0 dedication was applied by the Internet Archive uploader 'The Nostalgist777', not by the filmmaker Dan Lynch. Devin accepted that uploader-applied CC0 as-is on 2026-09-15 and ruled that filmmaker permission will not be pursued. The filmmaker did not license this footage and was not contacted.
Acquisition is not clearance. R14 stays open and release stays blocked for the OPS-04 review deck; the recognizable-people question is unresolved.
Only the one approved file was downloaded. No account, login, payment, terms click-through, CAPTCHA or bot-check bypass, no watermark removal, and no personal data in any request.

The raw Internet Archive metadata JSON was deliberately not committed: its uploader field contains a third party's personal email address. The uploader is recorded only by the display name shown on the item page.
The source is SD: 854x480 with a 632x480 active picture, so a 1080p timeline needs upscaling or a framing treatment. None was produced here.
The file carries an opus stereo audio track. It was probed but not auditioned; audio rights and content are unchecked.
The original is stored unmodified. The only derived files are the four PNG verification frames in evidence/frames/.
Genuine archival footage; no reenactment and no AI stand-in was created or commissioned.
